domain_label: Format, Verbosity & Persona Control (terse machine I/O)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
target deployment is machine-to-machine I/O where output tokens are consumed programmatically not by humans
constrained decoding (Willard & Louf 2023 Outlines approach) is available as an inference-time option
base model is a transformer decoder fine-tuneable via LoRA/full SFT; ToS review is always required
exclusions: human-facing chat verbosity and tone control outside machine I/O context
RLHF/DPO preference alignment for output quality beyond format
hardware-level inference optimization (quantization, batching, KV cache)
safety refusal behavior beyond structured abstention

competency_questions.question: What output schema contract governs the format that all enforcement mechanisms and evaluations align to?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FORMAT_SPEC defines schema, field semantics, enum tables, null policy

competency_questions.question: How is format compliance measured and what pass/fail thresholds gate deployment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EVAL_FORMAT defines parse rate and boilerplate metrics; FORMAT_REGRESSION defines CI gate

competency_questions.question: What mechanism provides hard syntactic format guarantees at inference time?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONSTRAINED_DECODE and LOGIT_BIAS describe grammar masking and token forcing

competency_questions.question: What recovery strategy handles format failures that pass through enforcement?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OUTPUT_PARSE_PIPELINE covers parse-error recovery and retry

competency_questions.question: How is output verbosity reduced without expensive runtime mechanisms?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STOP_SEQ and PROMPT_TEMPLATE describe zero-training verbosity controls; VERBOSITY_SFT describes SFT approach

competency_questions.question: How is SFT used to produce dense, machine-facing outputs with no boilerplate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VERBOSITY_SFT, DATA_CURATION_DENSE, and PEFT_FORMAT describe the SFT pipeline

competency_questions.question: How is a machine-facing persona installed without system-prompt token overhead?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PERSONA_CTRL describes persona baking via SFT; REPR_ENG covers representation-level steering

competency_questions.question: How are multiple output schemas served efficiently from a single model?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PEFT_FORMAT and MULTI_SCHEMA_ROUTING describe adapter-per-schema + routing

competency_questions.question: How does the system detect and signal low-confidence outputs without hallucinating?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ABSTENTION_CALIB describes structured abstention and ECE calibration; SEMANTIC_RETENTION covers detection

competency_questions.question: How is semantic information loss detected when output is compressed for token efficiency?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEMANTIC_RETENTION and TOKEN_EFFICIENCY define retention metric and compression Pareto

competency_questions.question: How is the context window token budget allocated across instructions, examples, and output?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTEXT_WINDOW_BUDGET defines allocation policy and truncation hierarchy

competency_questions.question: How is inference latency overhead from format enforcement monitored and bounded?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FORMAT_INFERENCE_LATENCY defines SLA and CONSTRAINED_DECODE overhead; CA_01 covers tradeoff

competency_questions.question: How is Goodhart's Law risk managed when optimizing format compliance metrics?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GOODHART_FORMAT and CA_07 describe joint metric gate

competency_questions.question: What must be verified about the base model before committing SFT compute for format specialization?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LICENSE_COMPLIANCE node and WF_01 define prerequisite license gate

glossary.definition: token-by-token restriction of autoregressive generation to grammar-legal continuations via logit masking
semantic information lost when compressing a verbose model output into a compact structured representation
chat-style preamble, apology, hedging, or explanation added by the model beyond the required structured output
model emits a structured null/abstain signal when internal confidence is below threshold, rather than hallucinating
fraction of generated outputs that are syntactically valid according to the target schema
activation delta added to a model's hidden states to steer output format style without weight updates
SFT training example with maximally compact structured output and no boilerplate; optimized for machine-to-machine information density
expected calibration error; measures alignment between model's expressed confidence and actual accuracy
lightweight PEFT (LoRA/IA3) adapter trained to specialize a base model's output to a particular schema or format style

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for format, verbosity, and persona control work units in absence of supplied datasets
Willard & Louf 2023 (Outlines) — constrained decoding via FSM over token vocabulary; key reference for grammar-constrained generation approach
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Willard B.T. & Louf R. 2023. Efficient Guided Generation for LLMs. arXiv:2307.09702
grounding_limits: original paper results not reproduced here; used as design reference only

source_registry.description: Tunstall, Werra, Wolf — NLP with Transformers (O'Reilly); reference for generation control (stop sequences, max_new_tokens, temperature, top-p)
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Tunstall L., von Werra L., Wolf T. 2022. Natural Language Processing with Transformers. O'Reilly Media.
grounding_limits: used as design reference; specific page numbers not reproduced here

nodes.definition: Define machine-facing output schemas (JSON, YAML, structured fields) and format contracts that downstream consumers depend on; includes enumerating legal value sets, field semantics, and null handling.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: consumer API or schema version changes

pros.claim: Establishes single source of truth for all format-enforcement downstream
pros.example: JSON schema v2020-12 used as contract for constrained decoder grammar

cons.claim: Schema too rigid stifles model generalization on edge inputs
cons.example: strict enum rejects valid rare values not foreseen in spec

failure_modes: under-specified nullable fields cause silent truncation
schema version drift breaks consumer parsers
acceptance_tests: schema round-trips losslessly through all downstream consumers
null/missing field policy documented and tested
revisit_triggers: downstream consumer schema changed
new field type or cardinality requirement introduced

nodes.definition: Enforce syntactic format constraints during autoregressive decoding by restricting the next-token distribution to a grammar-derived mask (FSM/CFG over legal continuations) — e.g., Outlines/lm-format-enforcer approach (Willard & Louf 2023).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: tokenizer or base model replaced; schema changes

pros.claim: Provides hard structural guarantee — decoder cannot emit syntactically invalid output
pros.example: Outlines converts JSON Schema to token-level FSM; invalid paths get -inf logit mask

cons.claim: Grammar compilation latency and cache size grow with schema complexity
cons.example: CFG with >50 fields compiles slowly; cache must be pre-warmed per schema

failure_modes: grammar state explosion on recursive or highly nested schemas
tokenizer-grammar misalignment causes false-negative mask on valid continuations
acceptance_tests: masked decoder produces parseable JSON on 100 consecutive test prompts
grammar compilation time <500ms for target schema set
no valid token incorrectly masked
revisit_triggers: schema changes requiring grammar recompile
tokenizer vocabulary updated (model upgrade)
new recursive schema type introduced

nodes.definition: Configure stop sequences, max_new_tokens caps, and truncation policies to prevent runaway generation and enforce output length budgets for token-efficient machine I/O.
outputs: generation config with stops and length caps

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: output schema delimiter set changes; context window resized

pros.claim: Cheapest mechanism to bound output length and delimit structured sections
pros.example: stop='</answer>' cuts multi-turn bleed at negligible cost

cons.claim: Stop sequences fail when model generates them inside valid content
cons.example: model outputs '<end>' inside a code block, halting generation prematurely

failure_modes: stop token appearing in valid content causing premature halt
max_tokens too low truncates required fields
acceptance_tests: stop-sequence coverage verified across all expected output formats
length distribution of valid outputs measured; cap set at 99th pctile+10%
revisit_triggers: output schema adds new delimiter tokens
length budget changes due to context window shift

nodes.definition: Curate dense I/O SFT pairs (input→compact structured output, no preamble/apology/explanation) and fine-tune a base model to suppress chat-style boilerplate; reduces token waste for machine-to-machine I/O.
outputs: SFT dataset of terse I/O pairs

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: verbosity target changes or safety review flags suppressed hedging

pros.claim: SFT directly shapes generation distribution toward compact machine output; generalizes better than prompt hacks
pros.example: model trained on 5K dense pairs drops average response length 60% with <1% content loss

cons.claim: Overfit terse SFT data degrades hedging and refusal capabilities needed for safety
cons.example: model loses calibrated uncertainty expression after aggressive brevity SFT

failure_modes: training on overly terse pairs suppresses valid hedging and abstention
distribution mismatch between SFT pairs and production inputs causes style regression
acceptance_tests: length reduction >40% on held-out machine I/O prompts vs base model
content retention F1 >0.95 on semantic equivalence eval
chat boilerplate rate <2% on 200-sample eval
revisit_triggers: production input distribution shifts materially
safety/alignment review flags suppressed uncertainty language
verbosity spec updated

nodes.definition: Remove or install a specific persona (assistant voice, disclaimer policy, role) through targeted SFT rather than system-prompt injection; enables persistent machine-facing identity with zero prompt overhead.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new persona requirement or multi-tenant deployment

pros.claim: Bakes persona into weights so no system-prompt tokens consumed at inference
pros.example: zero system-prompt overhead in production; saves ~200 tokens per call

cons.claim: Hard-coded persona resists dynamic override and complicates multi-tenant deployments
cons.example: single-persona model cannot serve different client voice requirements without re-finetune

failure_modes: persona bleeds through system-prompt override at inference time
training-time persona interferes with task-specific instruction following
acceptance_tests: persona absent from all 200 random production outputs without system prompt
task instruction following accuracy unchanged vs base within 2%
revisit_triggers: new persona or multi-tenant requirement introduced
safety policy changes persona constraints

nodes.definition: Train and configure the model to emit a structured abstention signal (e.g., {"answer":null,"reason":"low_confidence"}) rather than hallucinate when internal confidence is low; includes confidence elicitation via logit entropy or verbalized probability.
outputs: abstention rate and ECE eval report

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new task domain or calibration threshold revision

pros.claim: Prevents silent hallucination by converting uncertainty into machine-readable null signal
pros.example: structured null with reason field allows orchestrator to route to fallback

cons.claim: Miscalibrated threshold causes excess abstention and utility loss
cons.example: threshold too low causes 40% abstention rate; downstream pipeline stalls

failure_modes: over-abstention on medium-confidence inputs reducing throughput
under-abstention on genuinely uncertain outputs causing hallucination
entropy-based threshold unstable across task types
acceptance_tests: ECE <0.10 on held-out calibration set
abstention rate <15% on confident-domain queries
structured abstention output parses correctly 100%
revisit_triggers: new task domain with different confidence distribution
calibration threshold revised after downstream error analysis

nodes.definition: Apply logit bias (positive or negative weights to specific token IDs) at inference to steer or forbid tokens without grammar recompile; use for lightweight format nudging, token suppression, and controlled vocabulary restriction.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: tokenizer or model updated; schema changes

pros.claim: Runtime token steering with zero training cost; easily iterable
pros.example: adding -100 bias to '```' forces model off markdown in JSON-only mode

cons.claim: Logit bias is fragile — multi-token constructs need all constituent tokens biased; easy to miss
cons.example: biasing single 'null' token misses '_null_' multi-token variant

failure_modes: partial bias on multi-token sequences leaves escape paths
large negative bias causes probability mass redistribution to semantically wrong tokens
acceptance_tests: suppressed token absent from 500 generated samples
no semantic degradation measured on held-out content eval
revisit_triggers: model or tokenizer updated (token IDs change)
schema changes require different token suppression set

nodes.definition: Design system and user prompt templates that compactly convey format requirements (e.g., 'respond only with JSON matching schema X') without persona boilerplate; minimizes instruction token overhead while maximizing format compliance rate.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: context window budget changes or model instruction-following behavior shifts

pros.claim: Zero-training-cost format enforcement; fastest iteration loop for new schemas
pros.example: single-line 'Output only JSON' reduces markdown wrapping from 85% to 12%

cons.claim: Prompt-based format control is brittle for complex nested schemas; model ignores deep schema constraints
cons.example: model ignores 3rd-level nesting constraints on 22% of samples

failure_modes: verbose prompt templates consume context budget needed for content
model ignores format instructions on long documents where context is saturated
acceptance_tests: format compliance rate >90% on target schema
instruction token count <5% of context window budget
revisit_triggers: context window budget shifts
new schema requires additional instruction tokens
model updated with different instruction-following behavior

nodes.definition: Measure format compliance (parse rate, schema validity, boilerplate rate, length distribution) on held-out prompt sets using automated parsers and schema validators; defines pass/fail thresholds for CI/CD gates.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: schema changes or model checkpoint updated

pros.claim: Provides objective gating metric for format quality; prevents regressions in CI
pros.example: JSON parse rate drops from 99% to 71% caught before deployment

cons.claim: Eval covers syntax not semantics; high parse rate can coexist with wrong content
cons.example: 100% parse rate but field values semantically wrong undetected by format eval alone

failure_modes: eval set not representative of production prompt distribution
parse thresholds set too low mask progressive format degradation
acceptance_tests: parse rate >98% on target schema
boilerplate rate <3% on machine I/O eval set
CI gate blocks deployment if thresholds fail
revisit_triggers: output schema changes
new production prompt distribution detected
SFT data or model checkpoint updated

nodes.definition: Measure and minimize conversion loss: the gap between information content in the prompt/context and information preserved in the structured output; optimize token budget allocation across instruction, context, and output to minimize semantic loss per output token.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: context window or pricing model changes; output schema revised

pros.claim: Directly addresses machine-to-machine I/O cost; lower output tokens reduce latency and cost proportionally
pros.example: reducing avg output from 380 to 140 tokens cuts inference cost 63% with <2% semantic loss

cons.claim: Aggressive compression risks semantic loss on information-dense inputs; hard to detect without semantic eval
cons.example: removing 'qualifier' fields saves tokens but makes downstream decisions ambiguous

failure_modes: false efficiency from removing semantically load-bearing fields
token counting on prompt side ignores output token cost compounding across multi-turn pipelines
acceptance_tests: semantic retention F1 >0.93 at target compression ratio
output token reduction >30% vs untuned baseline on target task set
revisit_triggers: context window or pricing model changes
downstream consumer requires richer output fields

nodes.definition: Apply representation engineering (activation addition, reading vectors, steering vectors) to modify the model's internal representation to steer output format style (terse vs verbose, JSON-first vs prose) without weight updates.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: model architecture or family changes; new format style required

pros.claim: Enables runtime format switching without re-finetuning; lower cost than per-format checkpoint
pros.example: single steering vector shifts verbose→terse at layer 20 with <0.5% task accuracy loss

cons.claim: Steering vectors may generalize poorly across domains; require re-extraction per model family
cons.example: vector extracted on code domain does not transfer to medical domain format control

failure_modes: steering vector extracted from wrong layer causes incoherent outputs
additive steering conflicts with grammar constraint causing token mask conflicts
acceptance_tests: format compliance maintained >90% with steering vector applied
task accuracy delta <2% vs baseline on held-out eval
revisit_triggers: model architecture changes (new model family)
new format style target required beyond initial vector set

nodes.definition: Manage schema evolution (additive fields, deprecation, breaking changes) with explicit version fields in output, migration scripts, and consumer compatibility contracts to prevent silent breakage in multi-stage pipelines.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: field added, deprecated, or type changed in schema

pros.claim: Prevents silent breakage in multi-stage pipelines when output format evolves
pros.example: version field allows consumers to dispatch on schema version without redeployment

cons.claim: Over-engineering versioning adds latency from version negotiation and bloats output tokens
cons.example: 3-byte version field consumes 1% of tight token budget

failure_modes: breaking schema change not flagged as major version causes downstream parse errors
migration script not tested on edge-case null values
acceptance_tests: all consumers process old and new schema versions without error
breaking changes increment major version and trigger consumer notification
revisit_triggers: new field added or type changed
consumer deprecation deadline passed

nodes.definition: Train a lightweight LoRA/IA3 adapter on format-compliance SFT data, enabling format specialization without full fine-tune; multiple format adapters can be hot-swapped on a shared base for multi-schema deployment.
inputs: LoRA rank and target modules config

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: base model updated or format spec changes

pros.claim: PEFT allows multiple format styles on one base; each adapter ~10-50MB vs full checkpoint
pros.example: swap JSON adapter vs YAML adapter at runtime without serving two full 7B checkpoints

cons.claim: Adapter interference if format dimensions entangled with content dimensions in shared layers
cons.example: LoRA targeting attention-only misses MLP-driven boilerplate generation; incomplete format control

failure_modes: rank too low leaves residual boilerplate in output
adapter trained on too-narrow data distribution fails on prompt paraphrases
acceptance_tests: format compliance improvement >20pp over base model
adapter size <5% of base model parameter count
hot-swap latency <100ms
revisit_triggers: base model updated (adapter must be re-trained)
format spec changes requiring adapter re-training

nodes.definition: Collect and filter SFT training pairs where outputs are maximally dense machine-readable content (no hedges, no preambles, no apologies); apply quality filters (semantic retention, parse validity, length ratio) before training.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: production input distribution shifts; new schema added

pros.claim: High-quality dense pairs are the main lever for verbosity reduction; garbage in = verbose out
pros.example: filtering 40K pairs to 8K high-density pairs reduces verbosity more than increasing training steps on unfiltered data

cons.claim: Over-filtering removes naturally hedged content needed for calibrated abstention
cons.example: removing all 'I think' phrases eliminates valid low-confidence signals

failure_modes: semantic retention filter too aggressive removes valid qualifier fields
length ratio filter biased toward short inputs not representative of production
acceptance_tests: curation pipeline tested with 500-sample spot check
rejected pair analysis documented
curated dataset parse rate 100%
revisit_triggers: production prompt distribution shifts requiring re-curation
new output schema requires additional pair types

nodes.definition: Build the post-generation parsing pipeline that validates structured output, detects parse errors, and applies recovery strategies (retry with stricter prompt, extract partial JSON, invoke constrained decode fallback) to maximize end-to-end yield.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new parse error class in production; schema changes

pros.claim: Defense-in-depth: even with grammar enforcement, recovery pipeline catches edge failures
pros.example: partial JSON extraction recovers 94% of nearly-valid outputs without re-generation

cons.claim: Multi-stage recovery increases latency and complexity; masks upstream format enforcement failures
cons.example: slow retry loop adds 800ms p99 latency on parse failure

failure_modes: silent partial parse success returns wrong schema with no error signal
retry loop hits rate limits under production load
acceptance_tests: recovery pipeline handles top-5 error classes without human intervention
parse yield after recovery >99% on eval set
latency overhead <200ms at p95
revisit_triggers: new error class observed in production
schema changes requiring new recovery strategies

nodes.definition: Implement automated regression tests that run on every model checkpoint update or schema change, flagging format compliance drops >threshold and blocking deployment; includes canary eval on real production prompts.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: model checkpoint updated or schema changed

pros.claim: Prevents format regressions shipping to production; closes the train-then-forget loop
pros.example: CI gate catches 3 format regressions per quarter before they reach users

cons.claim: CI eval set staleness causes false passes when production prompt distribution drifts
cons.example: eval set from 6 months ago misses new prompt patterns; gate passes but production fails

failure_modes: eval set staleness causing false CI pass
threshold set too leniently misses gradual format degradation
acceptance_tests: CI gate blocks deployment when parse rate drops >3%
canary eval covers latest 2 weeks of production prompts
revisit_triggers: production prompt distribution drifts
format compliance SLA changes
new schema deployed

nodes.definition: Route incoming requests to the appropriate format-specialized model or adapter based on the required output schema; includes schema detection from request metadata and latency/cost-aware adapter selection.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new schema type added or adapter registry updated

pros.claim: Enables single serving infrastructure to support multiple output schemas without separate deployments
pros.example: one 7B base + 4 LoRA adapters serves JSON/YAML/CSV/Markdown schemas with 90% cost reduction vs 4 full models

cons.claim: Routing error sends request to wrong adapter; format mismatch causes silent downstream failure
cons.example: YAML adapter receives JSON schema request; output superficially valid but keys wrong

failure_modes: routing based on stale schema registry misroutes after schema update
adapter hot-swap latency violates real-time SLA
acceptance_tests: routing accuracy >99.5% on labeled test requests
adapter swap latency <50ms p99
routing error rate monitored and alerted
revisit_triggers: new schema type added
adapter registry updated
latency SLA changes

nodes.definition: Allocate tokens across system instruction, in-context examples (few-shot for format), input content, and output reserve within the context window limit; prioritize content over instruction overhead for dense machine I/O.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: context window limit changes or instruction set expanded

pros.claim: Explicit budget prevents instruction bloat from consuming output capacity
pros.example: policy: max 10% of window for instructions ensures 90% for content in 4K window

cons.claim: Fixed allocation policy fails on variable-length inputs requiring dynamic adjustment
cons.example: fixed 400-token instruction overhead leaves only 24 tokens for output on long document inputs

failure_modes: fixed allocation policy fails on variable-length inputs
few-shot examples for format consume more budget than they improve compliance
acceptance_tests: token allocation policy documented with priority order
dynamic truncation tested on inputs at 50%,90%,100% of window limit
revisit_triggers: context window limit changes (model upgrade)
instruction set expanded
new few-shot examples added

nodes.definition: Measure how much semantic information from the input is preserved in the compact structured output; uses field-level recall, information-theoretic metrics, or NLI-based entailment to detect lossy compression.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new task domain or compression ratio target changed

pros.claim: Closes the gap between syntactic format compliance and actual information preservation
pros.example: parse rate 99% but semantic retention 72%; retention eval catches silent information loss

cons.claim: NLI-based retention eval can be fooled by surface form matches that miss meaning
cons.example: entailment model marks paraphrase as retained but downstream task fails on field value

failure_modes: retention metric sensitive to phrasing not meaning
field checklist incomplete for novel input types
acceptance_tests: semantic retention F1 >0.90 on target task
lossy field rate <5% on production sample eval
revisit_triggers: new task domain introduced
compression ratio target changed
output schema revised

nodes.definition: Identify and mitigate Goodhart's Law failures in format optimization: models that achieve near-100% parse rate while degrading content quality; requires joint optimization of format compliance and semantic correctness metrics.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new format optimization objective or semantic quality baseline shifts

pros.claim: Prevents optimizing format metric at expense of actual utility; common failure mode in SFT for format
pros.example: model achieves 99% parse rate by emitting empty required fields that parse but convey nothing

cons.claim: Joint metric optimization increases eval cost and slows feedback loop
cons.example: dual metric CI gate doubles eval runtime; slows deployment cadence

failure_modes: format SFT causes model to game parse rate with minimal content
parse rate and semantic retention inversely coupled during aggressive format training
acceptance_tests: joint metric gate enforced in CI
Goodhart failure patterns documented and monitored
semantic quality maintained within 5% of pre-format-SFT baseline
revisit_triggers: new format optimization objective introduced
semantic quality baseline shifts after model update

nodes.definition: Profile and manage latency overhead from format enforcement mechanisms (grammar compilation cache miss, token masking per step, adapter swap); enforce SLA on format-related overhead as fraction of total inference time.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: hardware infra changes or schema distribution shifts

pros.claim: Prevents format enforcement from dominating inference time in high-throughput pipelines
pros.example: pre-warmed grammar cache reduces constrained decoding overhead from 35% to 3% of total latency

cons.claim: Latency optimization pressure leads to disabling grammar enforcement; removes hard format guarantees
cons.example: cache disabled for memory; reverts to unconstrained decode; parse rate drops 15%

failure_modes: grammar cache miss on novel schema at peak load causes latency spike
adapter swap synchronization blocks request queue
acceptance_tests: format enforcement overhead <10% of p99 inference latency
grammar cache hit rate >95% in production
revisit_triggers: production traffic schema distribution changes (new schema types increase cache misses)
hardware infra changes affecting memory for grammar cache

nodes.definition: Verify base model license and ToS permit fine-tuning for format specialization (some licenses restrict commercial SFT or derivative distribution); document compliance decision before committing to a fine-tuning path.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: base model license updated or deployment jurisdiction changes

pros.claim: License non-compliance discovered post-SFT forces checkpoint deletion and project restart; check upfront
pros.example: Llama 2 commercial license restrictions discovered after 3-week SFT run; checkpoint unusable

cons.claim: Upfront license review adds overhead and may require legal counsel
cons.example: legal review adds 1-week delay to project start

failure_modes: assuming permissive license without reading ToS
fine-tuning restriction buried in supplemental ToS not in main license file
acceptance_tests: license compliance decision documented before any SFT compute begins
legal or policy review completed for commercial deployments
revisit_triggers: base model license updated by provider
deployment jurisdiction changes (different license implications)

edges.label: format schema is source grammar for constrained decoder
schema delimiters inform stop sequence selection
schema defines target output structure for SFT data curation
schema content required to author format instructions
schema forbidden tokens informs logit bias set
schema content determines version management requirements
constrained decode output fed into format compliance eval
SFT checkpoint output evaluated for format compliance
verbosity reduction directly improves token efficiency
PEFT adapter trained on same dense I/O SFT data
aggressive verbosity SFT suppresses hedging needed for calibrated abstention; resolution: train with mixed abstention-positive pairs
edges.resolution_rule: maintain held-out abstention-positive examples in SFT mix; evaluate abstention rate and ECE jointly after verbosity SFT

edges.label: curated dense pairs are direct training input for verbosity SFT
same curated pairs used for PEFT adapter training
each PEFT adapter corresponds to a routable schema endpoint
format eval metrics and thresholds feed regression test CI gate
format compliance metric is subject to Goodhart gaming; joint eval needed
format eval and semantic retention must be co-evaluated
retention metric is the anti-Goodhart signal for format optimization
Goodhart checks must be included in CI regression gate
constrained decode reduces parse errors; pipeline handles residual failures
stop sequences define output boundaries used by parser
parse yield from pipeline is a key regression metric
grammar-constrained decoding adds per-step masking overhead; resolution: pre-warm grammar cache and profile overhead budget separately
edges.resolution_rule: pre-warm grammar cache at serving startup; enforce latency SLA as separate gate from format compliance

edges.label: adapter hot-swap adds latency not present in single-model serving; resolution: maintain adapter in GPU memory for hot schemas
edges.resolution_rule: keep top-N most-used adapters resident in GPU memory; swap only cold adapters

edges.label: steering vectors and grammar masks may conflict when vector pushes toward masked tokens; resolution: apply steering before logit masking in order
edges.resolution_rule: apply representation steering at hidden state level before final logit projection; grammar mask applied after projection

edges.label: license must be verified before SFT compute is committed
license must permit derivative fine-tuning before PEFT training
parser must handle all active schema versions
routing registry maps schema versions to adapter endpoints
persona-removal SFT built on same dense I/O pairs as verbosity SFT
abstention on low-confidence inputs improves downstream semantic retention by filtering hallucinated fields
prompt-only format control conflicts with grammar enforcement when instructions produce tokens outside grammar; resolution: treat grammar as hard constraint overriding prompt
edges.resolution_rule: grammar mask is authoritative; prompt instructions act as soft steering only; document override policy

edges.label: aggressive token reduction conflicts with semantic retention; resolution: set joint threshold (compression ratio, retention F1) and use Pareto frontier
edges.resolution_rule: optimize on Pareto frontier of token reduction vs retention F1; reject solutions below retention F1=0.90 regardless of token savings

edges.label: explicit budget management enables measurement of actual token efficiency gains
steering vectors for verbosity may interfere with SFT-learned distribution; test joint effect before combining
edges.resolution_rule: ablate steering vector contribution independently before combining with SFT checkpoint; use format compliance eval to detect interference

conflict_axes.description: Hard format guarantees (grammar-constrained decoding) add per-step masking overhead; relaxing to soft enforcement (prompt+SFT) reduces latency but loses guarantees.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: use grammar enforcement for high-risk structured fields; prompt-only for low-risk free-text sub-fields; pre-warm cache to minimize overhead

conflict_axes.description: Aggressive brevity SFT suppresses hedging language that encodes uncertainty; calibrated abstention requires model to express low confidence.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: include abstention-positive (structured null+reason) pairs in SFT mix; evaluate ECE jointly with verbosity metric

conflict_axes.description: Maximizing token compression risks dropping semantically load-bearing fields; joint optimization required.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: set minimum semantic retention F1=0.90 as hard constraint; optimize token reduction on feasible frontier only

conflict_axes.description: Strict schemas (closed enum, required fields) guarantee parsability but prevent model from expressing valid edge-case content.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: use open-ended string fields for edge-case content; apply enums only to fields with closed value sets

conflict_axes.description: Representation steering vectors push hidden states toward format targets but may conflict with token-level grammar masks applied at logit layer.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: apply steering at hidden state level before logit projection; grammar mask is downstream hard constraint and takes priority

conflict_axes.description: Baking a specific persona into SFT weights eliminates runtime overhead but prevents dynamic persona switching for multi-tenant deployments.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: use PEFT adapter per persona for multi-tenant; bake persona in weights only for single-tenant deployments with stable identity requirement

conflict_axes.description: Optimizing format compliance metrics (parse rate) can cause model to game metric by emitting syntactically valid but semantically empty outputs.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: gate on joint metric: parse rate AND semantic retention F1; never gate on parse rate alone

conflict_axes.description: Committing GPU compute to SFT before license review risks non-compliant checkpoints that must be deleted; irreversibility is high.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: license compliance check is a hard prerequisite gate before any SFT or PEFT compute; no exceptions

conflict_axes.description: When grammar enforcement overrides prompt-based format instructions, model behavior may surprise users who expect prompt to be authoritative.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: document grammar-as-hard-constraint policy; prompt instructions act as soft steering; grammar override is explicit and logged

conflict_axes.description: CI eval sets become stale as production prompt distribution drifts; stale eval gives false CI passes while production format fails.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: refresh canary eval set from last 2 weeks of production prompts on each CI run; flag staleness if distribution shift detected

edge_cases.description: Recursive or self-referential JSON schema causes grammar state explosion, making FSM compilation infeasible at runtime.
edge_cases.trigger: output schema contains recursive $ref or unbounded nesting depth
edge_cases.recommended_action: flatten recursive schemas to bounded depth; use JSON string field with post-parse validation for recursive sub-structures

edge_cases.description: Model generates stop sequence inside a valid string field value, causing premature truncation of required output.
edge_cases.trigger: stop token string appears in domain-specific content (e.g., XML tags in code output)
edge_cases.recommended_action: use schema-derived unique delimiters unlikely to appear in content; add output_parse_pipeline recovery for premature stop detection

edge_cases.description: Tokenizer update in base model changes token IDs, invalidating pre-compiled grammar FSM and logit bias token mappings.
edge_cases.trigger: base model or tokenizer updated (new BPE vocab)
edge_cases.recommended_action: version-lock grammar cache and logit bias configs to tokenizer hash; auto-invalidate and recompile on tokenizer change

edge_cases.description: Aggressive verbosity SFT on domain-narrow data causes out-of-domain format regression: model produces correct format on training distribution but reverts to verbose output on novel inputs.
edge_cases.trigger: production prompt distribution shifts outside SFT training distribution
edge_cases.recommended_action: curate diverse SFT data; include canary prompts from multiple domains; monitor format compliance by input domain in production

edge_cases.description: Calibrated abstention threshold miscalibrated for a new task domain: model abstains too frequently, reducing useful throughput below acceptable levels.
edge_cases.trigger: model deployed on new task domain with different entropy distribution
edge_cases.recommended_action: re-calibrate abstention threshold per task domain; maintain per-domain ECE dashboards

edge_cases.description: PEFT adapter hot-swap under high concurrency causes race condition where request receives mismatched adapter during swap.
edge_cases.trigger: concurrent requests during adapter swap for new schema type
edge_cases.recommended_action: use atomic adapter swap with request queuing; maintain N+1 adapter slots to allow zero-downtime swap

edge_cases.description: Representation steering vector extracted from a different task domain does not generalize to production inputs, causing incoherent format steering.
edge_cases.trigger: steering vector extracted on code domain applied to medical/legal text
edge_cases.recommended_action: extract and validate steering vectors per deployment domain; do not assume cross-domain transfer

edge_cases.description: Schema version mismatch between model checkpoint (trained on v1) and consumer (expecting v2) causes silent field-mapping errors undetected by parse rate metric.
edge_cases.trigger: schema version incremented without corresponding model retraining
edge_cases.recommended_action: include schema version field in model output; add version-aware test cases in CI regression gate

edge_cases.description: Goodhart failure: model achieves 100% parse rate by emitting required field keys with empty string values, satisfying schema validator but conveying no information.
edge_cases.trigger: format SFT optimized on parse rate without semantic retention joint metric
edge_cases.recommended_action: add non-empty field value check to format eval; gate on semantic retention F1 jointly with parse rate

edge_cases.description: Context window budget overflow: fixed instruction+few-shot overhead exceeds available tokens on max-length production inputs, causing output truncation before required fields are generated.
edge_cases.trigger: production input length at 95th+ percentile combined with fixed-overhead prompt template
edge_cases.recommended_action: implement dynamic instruction truncation hierarchy; measure token overflow rate in production; set alert threshold

edge_cases.description: License non-compliance discovered after GPU-hours of SFT; checkpoint must be deleted and project restarted on a compliant base model.
edge_cases.trigger: license review skipped or incomplete before SFT begins
edge_cases.recommended_action: license compliance is a mandatory blocking gate before any fine-tuning compute; document approval in project record

edge_cases.description: Multi-schema routing sends request to wrong adapter because schema tag was absent or ambiguous in request metadata.
edge_cases.trigger: upstream system sends requests without schema tag or with deprecated tag
edge_cases.recommended_action: implement schema detection fallback using output schema inference from request content; log and alert on tag-absent requests

workflow.description: Confirm base model license permits intended fine-tuning and commercial use before committing any compute.
workflow.gate: license compliance decision documented and approved

workflow.description: Author output schema (JSON/YAML), enumerate legal values, define null policy, and establish version v1.
workflow.gate: schema round-trips through all target consumers without error

workflow.description: Write compact system instructions; measure instruction token overhead; set dynamic truncation policy.
workflow.gate: instruction token count <10% of context window; format compliance >80% on baseline model

workflow.description: Select stop sequences from schema delimiters; set max_new_tokens at 99th pctile of valid output length +10%.
workflow.gate: no premature stops on 500-sample test; length cap not triggered on valid outputs

workflow.description: Collect and filter SFT pairs for dense machine output; apply semantic retention and parse validity filters.
workflow.gate: 100% parse rate on curated set; semantic retention F1 >0.92

workflow.description: Fine-tune on curated dense pairs to suppress boilerplate and set machine-facing persona; include abstention-positive pairs in mix.
workflow.gate: verbosity reduction >40%; boilerplate rate <2%; ECE <0.12 on calibration set

workflow.description: Train LoRA adapters per output schema for multi-schema deployment; validate each adapter independently.
workflow.gate: format compliance >20pp improvement over base; adapter size <5% of base parameters

workflow.description: Compile grammar from output schema; pre-warm cache; validate no valid tokens masked; measure masking overhead.
workflow.gate: grammar cache hit rate >95%; overhead <10% of inference latency; 100 consecutive parse successes

workflow.description: Set and validate confidence threshold for structured abstention; measure ECE and abstention rate on calibration set.
workflow.gate: ECE <0.10; abstention rate <15% on confident-domain queries

workflow.description: Implement parse validation, error recovery, and retry strategies; test on top-5 error classes.
workflow.gate: parse yield after recovery >99%; latency overhead <200ms at p95

workflow.description: Run joint format compliance and semantic retention eval; check for Goodhart failures; compute token efficiency.
workflow.gate: parse rate >98%; retention F1 >0.90; token reduction >30%; no Goodhart failure patterns

workflow.description: Wire eval metrics into CI/CD; set deployment-blocking thresholds; configure canary eval refresh from recent production prompts.
workflow.gate: CI gate blocks on parse rate drop >3%; canary set refreshed from last 2 weeks of production

dominance_rules.rule: LICENSE_COMPLIANCE must pass before any SFT or PEFT training compute is committed; no exceptions regardless of schedule pressure.
dominance_rules.rationale: Non-compliant checkpoint deletion wastes all subsequent compute and may create legal liability.

dominance_rules.rule: Grammar-constrained decoding is authoritative over prompt-based format instructions; grammar mask overrides any conflicting prompt instruction.
dominance_rules.rationale: Hard syntactic guarantees cannot coexist with soft prompt steering as equal-priority mechanisms; grammar must dominate.

dominance_rules.rule: Format compliance metric gate must always be paired with semantic retention F1 gate; parse rate alone is never a sufficient deployment criterion.
dominance_rules.rationale: Goodhart failure (high parse rate, empty content) is undetectable by parse rate alone.

dominance_rules.rule: Abstention-positive SFT pairs must be included in verbosity SFT data mix before training; do not curate them out as 'non-terse'.
dominance_rules.rationale: Verbosity SFT without abstention examples eliminates calibrated uncertainty expression needed for reliable machine I/O.

dominance_rules.rule: Grammar cache must be pre-warmed at serving startup for all known schemas; do not compile on first request under load.
dominance_rules.rationale: Cold grammar compilation under load causes latency spikes that breach SLA and may trigger cascading retries.

dominance_rules.rule: Schema version field must be present in every model output; consumers must dispatch on version before parsing fields.
dominance_rules.rationale: Silent schema version mismatch causes field-mapping errors that are undetectable by syntactic parse rate.

dominance_rules.rule: Token compression ratio target must be bounded below by semantic retention F1>=0.90; no solution on the infeasible side is acceptable regardless of business pressure.
dominance_rules.rationale: Lossless machine I/O is only valuable if information content is preserved; lossy compression defeats the purpose.

dominance_rules.rule: PEFT adapter training must be preceded by FORMAT_SPEC finalization; adapters trained on pre-final schema must be retrained after schema changes.
dominance_rules.rationale: Adapter trained on wrong schema creates format-schema mismatch that produces high parse rate on old schema but fails on new schema.

dominance_rules.rule: CI format regression gate must refresh canary eval set from recent production prompts at least every 2 weeks; stale eval set overrides must be logged and reviewed.
dominance_rules.rationale: Stale eval sets give false CI passes while production format degrades; prompt distribution drift is a continuous risk.

dominance_rules.rule: Representation steering vectors must be validated per deployment domain before production use; do not assume cross-domain transfer of format steering vectors.
dominance_rules.rationale: Domain-specific activation patterns mean a vector effective on code format control may be harmful on medical text format control.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not begin SFT data curation before FORMAT_SPEC is finalized; schema changes after curation require full re-curation.
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-curation cost when schema changes post-curation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not deploy a format adapter trained on schema v(N) to serve requests for schema v(N+1); always retrain adapter after schema version increment.
anti_rework_rules.prevents: silent field-mapping errors from schema-adapter version mismatch

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not set CI gate thresholds before collecting a calibration sample of >=200 production outputs; threshold set on too-small sample requires revision after production data available.
anti_rework_rules.prevents: threshold revision requiring CI reconfiguration and re-baselining

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not configure logit bias token IDs before tokenizer version is locked; tokenizer update invalidates all token ID mappings.
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-mapping all logit bias configs after tokenizer update

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not finalize context window budget allocation before measuring actual instruction token counts from the finalized prompt template; estimate-based allocation frequently requires revision.
anti_rework_rules.prevents: context window overflow discovered in production requiring emergency truncation policy update

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not skip semantic retention eval during format SFT; Goodhart failures discovered post-deployment require full retraining.
anti_rework_rules.prevents: full retraining after Goodhart failure discovered in production

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not merge persona SFT and verbosity SFT into a single training run without first ablating each independently; entangled effects are hard to debug post-training.
anti_rework_rules.prevents: debugging entangled persona/verbosity effects requiring separate re-runs

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not configure multi-schema routing before all target adapters are validated; routing a request to an unvalidated adapter produces undetected format failures.
anti_rework_rules.prevents: silent format failures on production traffic before adapters are validated

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not assume abstention threshold calibrated on one task domain applies to a new domain; re-calibrate per domain before production deployment.
anti_rework_rules.prevents: over-abstention or under-abstention failure discovered in production on new domain

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not remove stop sequences or relax length caps without first measuring impact on output length distribution and downstream parse pipeline; silent truncation failures are difficult to trace.
anti_rework_rules.prevents: downstream parse failures from stop sequence removal discovered across multiple dependent systems

iteration_protocol.trigger: format compliance (parse rate) drops >3% from baseline in CI
iteration_protocol.action: run FORMAT_REGRESSION canary; check if schema changed, model updated, or prompt template modified; re-run EVAL_FORMAT on canary

iteration_protocol.trigger: semantic retention F1 drops below 0.90 on eval set
iteration_protocol.action: run SEMANTIC_RETENTION diagnostic; check if DATA_CURATION_DENSE over-filtered qualifier fields; inspect lossy field list; adjust curation filter or SFT data mix

iteration_protocol.trigger: abstention rate exceeds 20% on confident-domain queries
iteration_protocol.action: re-calibrate ABSTENTION_CALIB threshold; check if VERBOSITY_SFT suppressed uncertainty language; re-run ECE eval on calibration set

iteration_protocol.trigger: grammar compilation failure or cache miss rate >10%
iteration_protocol.action: inspect CONSTRAINED_DECODE for schema recursion or complexity growth; pre-warm cache for newly added schemas; profile per-schema compilation time

iteration_protocol.trigger: output token count regresses to pre-SFT baseline on production sample
iteration_protocol.action: check if new prompt types triggered verbose mode; inspect VERBOSITY_SFT eval on new prompt distribution; consider targeted data augmentation

iteration_protocol.trigger: Goodhart failure pattern detected (high parse rate, low semantic retention)
iteration_protocol.action: add non-empty field value checks to EVAL_FORMAT; add semantic retention gate to CI; review VERBOSITY_SFT training objective for parse-rate gaming

iteration_protocol.trigger: PEFT adapter hot-swap latency exceeds 100ms p99
iteration_protocol.action: profile FORMAT_INFERENCE_LATENCY; increase resident adapter count in GPU memory; optimize adapter swap protocol

iteration_protocol.trigger: schema version mismatch errors appear in output parse pipeline logs
iteration_protocol.action: inspect SCHEMA_VERSION registry; verify consumers updated to dispatch on version field; add version-aware test cases to FORMAT_REGRESSION CI

iteration_protocol.trigger: representation steering vector causes incoherent format outputs on new domain
iteration_protocol.action: re-extract REPR_ENG steering vector on domain-representative contrastive pairs; validate on held-out domain eval before re-deploying

iteration_protocol.trigger: context window overflow detected on production inputs at 95th percentile length
iteration_protocol.action: measure CONTEXT_WINDOW_BUDGET utilization by component; implement dynamic truncation hierarchy; reduce PROMPT_TEMPLATE instruction tokens

priority_rationale: LICENSE_COMPLIANCE first as blocking irreversibility gate; FORMAT_SPEC second as contract all mechanisms depend on; hard enforcement (CONSTRAINED_DECODE) before SFT approaches; SFT pipeline ordered by dependency (data→train→eval); evaluation and risk nodes (GOODHART, SEMANTIC_RETENTION) before operational infrastructure; lightweight mechanisms (STOP_SEQ, LOGIT_BIAS, REPR_ENG) last as iterative overlays

change_control.review_policy: human review required for nodes with risk_if_wrong>=0.80 or irreversibility>=0.70

test_cases.input_summary: 50 schema-constrained prompts; all outputs must parse as valid JSON
100 machine-IO prompts before and after verbosity SFT
200 prompts evaluated for parse rate AND semantic retention jointly
calibration set with known high/low confidence inputs
